sentences.text:
Applicant :- Rohit Gond
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P.And 3 Others

Counsel for Applicant :- Prakhar Saran Srivastava,Shashi Bhushan Kunwar Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1. Sri Jhamman Ram, learned AGA apprised the Court that on 27.7.2023, notice has been served to the informant.
Despite service of notice, none appeared on behalf of the informant.

2. Heard Sri Kamal Krishna, learned Senior Advocate holding brief of SriShashi Bhushan Kunwar,
learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Jhamman Ram, learned AGA for the State-respondent.
3.

The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
240 of 2023, under Sections 363, 366, 376(3) IPC and 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Kotwali,
District Ballia, during pendency of the trial in the court below.
4. FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant under section 363 IPC and according to the FIR, applicant enticed away the daughter of the informant aged about 15 years.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the entire allegations made against the applicant are totally false and baseless and actually, prosecutrix is a major girl aged about 18 years and Rohit Gond vs State Of U.P.And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49733053/
1 applicant and prosecutrix loved each other and prosecutrix according to her own wish had gone alongwith the applicant and also performed marriage with him and this fact is even evident from both the statements of the prosecutrix recorded under sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
6.

sentences.text: He further submitted that prosecutrix in her statement recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C. stated that she at present is studying in class-9 and her date of birth is 20.9.2005 and according to the date of birth disclosed by her she was around 17 years old at the time of incident but during investigation Investigating Officer procured transfer certificate of primary school Chauk, Paschimi Nagar, Balia and according to the transfer certificate of the prosecutrix it appears that she studied in primary school Balia from class 2nd to class 5th and as per school record, her date of birth is 5.5.2009 and therefore, there is variations of about five years in the date of birth of prosecutrix mentioned in the primary school Balia and in her statement recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C.
, therefore, merely on the basis of school leaving certificate/transfer certificate of prosecutrix of class 5, it cannot be said that prosecutrix was around 14 years old.

7. He further submitted that even as per observation made by the Apex Court in the case of [P.
Yuvaprakash Vs. State represented by Inspector of Polic (Criminal Appeal No. (S). 1898 of 2023 dated 18.7.2023], the date of birth disclosed in the school leaving certificate/transfer certificate of the prosecutrix is not admissible.

sentences.text: 8. He further submitted that applicant is also about 20 years old boy and it is a case of love affair and applicant is having no criminal history and he is in jail in the present matter since 28.5.2023.

9. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that as per the primary school Balia, the date of birth of the prosecutrix is 5.5.2009 and therefore, at the time of incident, she was hardly 14 years old but could not dispute the fact that in the statement recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C. prosecutrix herself disclosed her age as 20.9.2005 and she also stated that she studied in class 9 and therefore, there is a dispute with regard to the date of birth of the prosecutrix.
10. He further could not dispute the fact that prosecutrix in her both the statements recorded under sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. did not make any allegation against the applicant.
11. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

12. Although from the transfer certificate of primary school Paschimi Nagar, Ballia it appears that date of birth of the prosecutrix is 5.5.2009 and at the time of incident, she was hardly 14 years old but in the statement under section 164 Cr.P.C. prosecutrix disclosed her date of birth as 20.9.2005 and she further stated that she studied up to class 9 and as per the date of birth disclosed by the prosecutrix in her statement recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C. her age at the time of incident was around 17 years, therefore, there is a dispute with regard to the correct date of birth of the prosecutrix and at this stage, this Court cannot give any finding in this regard.
13.

Further, during investigation, ossification test of the prosecutrix was not conducted and prosecutrix in her both the statements recorded under sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. did not make Rohit Gond vs State Of U.P.And 3 Others

14.
Law is settled that bail application should not be rejected either for punitive or preventive purposes.

15. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
16. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

17. Let the applicant-Rohit Gond, be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
18. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

19. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
